title: Five Great White Grapes
quiz.0.question: What is Italy's biggest-exporting white wine?
quiz.0.explanation: Pinot Grigio is Italy's biggest-exporting white wine and is very popular on the global market.
quiz.1.question: Which grape is Soave mainly made from?
quiz.1.explanation: Soave (especially Soave Classico DOC) is made mainly from Garganega, known for its almond notes.
quiz.2.question: Which grape is famous for its distinctive amphora-shaped (anfora) bottle?
quiz.2.explanation: Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi has traditionally been sold in an amphora-shaped bottle (often likened to a fish), very recognisable.
quiz.3.question: What are Vermentino's signature flavours?
quiz.3.explanation: Vermentino grows in coastal areas and shows clear citrus, sea-breeze and savoury salinity, its hallmark.
slides.0.title: 🍾 Italy's Five Great White Grapes
slides.0.subtitle: A fresh world from Pinot Grigio to Vermentino
slides.1.title: 🏆 The Five Great White Grapes at a Glance
slides.1.content:
Five grapes covering the full style spectrum of Italian white wine, from Friuli's crisp Pinot Grigio to Sardinia's coastal Vermentino, from the mass market to top collectibles — there is a right choice for every occasion

🌟 Pinot Grigio — The International Star

From fine, crisp Friuli/Trentino wines to the Veneto mass market, Italy's biggest-exporting white. Light and easy, medium-high acid, green apple and pear, drunk young.

🌾 Trebbiano + 🍇 Garganega — Neutral Workhorse & Soave's Finest

Trebbiano: Italy's most widely planted white grape, called Ugni Blanc in France, a light, high-acid everyday wine and a raw material for balsamic vinegar. Garganega: the soul of Soave, with a distinctive bitter-almond finish, complexity and ageing potential.

💎 Verdicchio + 🌊 Vermentino — Twin Stars of Minerality and the Coast

Verdicchio: the mineral jewel of Marche, in an amphora-shaped bottle, high acid and minerality, perfect with seafood. Vermentino: Sardinia's coastal star, called Rolle in France, with a salty, savoury Mediterranean character.

slides.2.title: 🌟 Pinot Grigio — The International Star
slides.2.content:
"Grey Pinot" (Pinot Gris / Pinot Grigio), Italy's biggest-exporting white wine — a crisp, light international star, from top Friuli wines to the mass market, covering every choice from entertaining to everyday

🎨 Grape Profile

Colour: pale yellow with green tints, clear (the skin-contact ramato version is copper-coloured)

Aromas: green apple, pear, citrus, white flowers, honeysuckle; quality versions show honey and almond

Palate: medium to high acidity, light to medium body, fresh and easy, 12-13.5%

Regions: Friuli-Venezia Giulia (the best), Trentino-Alto Adige (fresh, high altitude), Veneto (mass market)

🍷 Key Wines & Food

Friuli Pinot Grigio DOC: the finest, mineral and crisp, the famous Jermann estate, ageing 3-5 years

Trentino-Alto Adige DOC: fresh and high-altitude, more floral and mineral, balanced and elegant

Delle Venezie DOC: mass market, easy and approachable, drunk young

Food: salads, antipasto, steamed fish, seafood, white meat, pasta, sushi

Hallmark: Italy's biggest-exporting white and the world's most popular Italian white, best young within 1-3 years

slides.3.title: 🌾 Trebbiano — The Volume Giant
slides.3.content:
Italy's most widely planted white grape, called Ugni Blanc in France — high-yielding, high in acid and light, a good partner for everyday wine and an important raw material for Modena's balsamic vinegar and French Cognac

🎨 Grape Profile

Colour: pale yellow, clear, usually very light

Aromas: neutral and light, green apple, lemon, white peach; quality versions show white flowers and minerality

Palate: high acidity (its greatest strength), light to medium body, crisp and uncomplicated, 11-12.5%

Character: its high acidity is a natural strength, making it a good blending base; called Ugni Blanc in France, it is the core base grape for Cognac

🍷 Key Wines & Food

Trebbiano d'Abruzzo DOC: Abruzzo's most important white; the top producer Valentini's version can age 10+ years, astonishing in quality

Orvieto DOC (blend): Umbria's famous wine, blended on a Trebbiano base, sometimes impressively mineral

Lugana DOC: Trebbiano di Lugana (also called Turbiana), by Lake Garda; despite the name it is closer to Verdicchio, floral and mineral

Food: fried seafood (fritto misto), light fish, salads, antipasto — crisp, easy everyday drinking

Balsamic vinegar: Trebbiano is an important raw material for Modena's traditional balsamic vinegar (Aceto Balsamico Tradizionale)

slides.4.title: 🍇 Garganega — The Soul of Soave
slides.4.content:
Veneto's elegant white grape, the soul of Soave — a distinctive almond (mandorla) finish, white peach, apricot and blossom, and top Soave Classico shows astonishing complexity after 10+ years

🎨 Grape Profile

Colour: pale yellow-green, very clear, turning golden with age

Aromas: white peach, apricot, almond blossom, honeysuckle, lemon; its hallmark: an almond (mandorla) finish, unique

Palate: medium to high acidity, mineral, medium to full body, a slightly bitter almond finish, 11.5-13%

Region: Veneto (near Verona); the volcanic basalt soils of Soave Classico add mineral complexity

🍷 Key Wines & Food

Soave Classico DOC: the historic heart, at least 70% Garganega by law, top estates Gini / Pieropan, strong ageing potential

Soave Superiore DOCG: hillside vineyards only, lower yields, complex and elegant

Recioto di Soave DOCG: a sweet white from dried grapes, rich with almond and honey, rivalling France's Sauternes

Food: freshwater perch, roast chicken (pollo arrosto), light pasta, vegetable dishes

Ageing: Soave Classico 3-8 years, single vineyards 5-12 years; the almond note grows with age

slides.5.title: 💎 Verdicchio — The Mineral Jewel of Marche
slides.5.content:
The mineral jewel of Marche, famous for its distinctive amphora-shaped bottle — high acidity and minerality with a herbal, slightly bitter finish, central Italy's most distinctive white and a natural partner for seafood

🎨 Grape Profile

Colour: pale yellow-green, clear and bright (the name Verdicchio comes from verde = green)

Aromas: lemon, green apple, white flowers, minerality, a hint of sea salt; hazelnut and nuts develop with age

Palate: high acidity, vivid minerality, light to medium body, a slightly bitter finish (a varietal trait), 11.5-13%

Hallmark: the amphora (anfora) bottle popular since the 1950s, often likened to a fish, is the most recognisable traditional packaging of Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi

🍷 Key Wines & Food

Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi DOC: the most famous, the coastal hills of Marche, top estates Umani Ronchi / Bucci, crisp and mineral

Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi Classico Superiore: a more complex version with stronger minerality

Verdicchio di Matelica DOC: the inland mountain version, fuller-bodied with more intense minerality

Food: oysters / shellfish (a natural match), fried seafood, Asian cuisine; its minerality resonates with the savour of seafood

Ageing: standard wines 3-5 years, Riserva 5-10 years, gaining complexity with time

slides.6.title: 🌊 Vermentino — Star of the Coast
slides.6.content:
The star of the Mediterranean coast and the pride of Sardinia — salty minerality, citrus and sea breeze, the southern islands' most distinctive contribution to the world of white wine and the soulmate of a seafood feast

🎨 Grape Profile

Colour: pale gold, bright, slightly deeper than other white grapes

Aromas: citrus (grapefruit/lime), fresh grass, Mediterranean herbs (rosemary), sea-salt minerality, honey

Palate: medium-high acidity, vivid minerality, savoury salinity (a coastal trait), medium body, 12-14%

Main regions: Sardinia (the most famous), Liguria (around Cinque Terre), the Tuscan coast

🍷 Key Wines & Food

Vermentino di Gallura DOCG: northern Sardinia, Italy's finest Vermentino, with granite soils giving intense minerality

Vermentino di Sardegna DOC: the whole island of Sardinia, crisp and easy, excellent value

Colli di Luni Vermentino DOC: on the Liguria/Tuscany border, an elegant, refined coastal style

Food: all kinds of seafood (a natural match), grilled sea bass (branzino), Mediterranean salads, fish soup (zuppa di pesce)

French name: Rolle, widely grown in Provence, a main grape of Côtes de Provence whites

slides.7.title: 📊 The Five Grapes Compared
slides.7.content:
From choosing a bottle to food pairing — understanding how the five white grapes relate opens the door to the world of Italian white wine

✨ Crisp and Easy

Pinot Grigio: medium-high acid and light, green apple and pear, the biggest exporter, a versatile introduction, 1-3 years

Trebbiano: high acid, light and neutral, a base for everyday blends and raw material for balsamic vinegar, 1-2 years

Getting started: begin with Pinot Grigio to get to know the crisp character of Italian whites

Rule of thumb: drink fresh, with antipasto and light food

💎 Mineral and Complex

Garganega (Soave): medium-high acid, medium-full body, signature almond, elegant ageing, 3-12 years

Verdicchio: high acid, mineral and herbal, a slightly bitter finish, perfect with seafood, 3-10 years

Vermentino: medium-high acid, coastal salinity, Mediterranean character, 2-5 years

Going further: explore Garganega in Soave Classico and Verdicchio to discover the depth of Italian whites

slides.8.title: 🍽️ Food Pairing Suggestions
slides.8.content:
Italian white wine's natural bond with the sea — each of the five white grapes forms perfect pairings with different seafood, light dishes and Mediterranean food

🌟 Pinot Grigio / Trebbiano

Pair with: salads / antipasto / fried seafood
Their crisp, light style is perfect before a meal or with light food. Friuli Pinot Grigio with raw fish is as refreshing as spring water; Trebbiano's high acidity with fritto misto cuts the grease superbly — the most common pairing in Italian seaside trattorias.

🍇 Garganega (Soave)

Pair with: grilled perch / chicken dishes / vegetable risotto
Almond notes and minerality give Soave Classico remarkable versatility with food. Garganega's apricot blossom with chicken risotto is the most classic Veneto pairing, while sweet Recioto di Soave is a superb match for foie gras.

💎 Verdicchio

Pair with: oysters / shellfish / Asian cuisine
Verdicchio was born for seafood. Its high acid and minerality resonate perfectly with the salty savour of oysters; its slightly bitter finish also makes Asian food (Japanese steamed fish, miso soup) a great match. The soul pairing of Marche's fishing ports.

🌊 Vermentino

Pair with: grilled fish / Mediterranean salads / fish soup
Its coastal salinity makes Vermentino a natural partner for Mediterranean food. Sardinian roast sea bass (branzino) with Vermentino di Gallura is the island's finest lunchtime, savour meeting savour in perfect harmony.

slides.10.title: 🎓 Key Takeaways
slides.10.points.0: ✓ Pinot Grigio is Italy's biggest-exporting white, crisp and light; Friuli-Venezia Giulia produces the highest-quality versions, and it is the world's most popular Italian white
slides.10.points.1: ✓ Trebbiano is Italy's most widely planted white grape, called Ugni Blanc in France — the core base wine for Cognac and an important raw material for Modena's traditional balsamic vinegar
slides.10.points.2: ✓ Garganega is the core grape of Soave DOC (at least 70% by law), famous for its distinctive almond (mandorla) finish; top Soave Classico can age 10+ years
slides.10.points.3: ✓ Verdicchio is Marche's signature mineral white, its name from verde (green); its traditional amphora-shaped bottle is one of Italy's most recognisable bottle designs
slides.10.points.4: ✓ Vermentino is a coastal grape of Sardinia and Liguria, called Rolle in France, with a distinctive sea-salt minerality; Vermentino di Gallura DOCG is the top version
slides.10.points.5: ✓ A beginner's path: Pinot Grigio / Trebbiano (crisp and easy) → Verdicchio / Vermentino (mineral character) → Garganega Soave Classico (elegant and complex)
slides.10.points.6: ✓ The defining trait of Italian whites: generally high acidity, a natural match for seafood, antipasto, pasta and the Mediterranean diet
slides.10.points.7: ✓ Where the five grapes grow: Friuli / Veneto (Pinot Grigio) → widely in the centre (Trebbiano) → Veneto (Garganega) → Marche (Verdicchio) → Sardinia (Vermentino)
slides.10.points.8: ✓ Pairing rules: mineral whites (Verdicchio / Vermentino) with seafood; crisp styles (Pinot Grigio) with light food; complex, age-worthy styles (Garganega) with white meat
slides.11.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
slides.11.questions.0.question: Which Italian white grape is the most exported and most popular with international consumers?
slides.11.questions.0.explanation: Pinot Grigio is Italy's most exported white grape; the crisp versions from the north (especially Friuli) are crowd-pleasing, sell strongly in markets such as the US and UK, and represent Italian white wine internationally.
slides.11.questions.1.question: Which statements about Trebbiano (Ugni Blanc) are correct? (Select all that apply)
slides.11.questions.1.options.0: A. One of Italy's most widely planted white grapes
slides.11.questions.1.options.1: B. Light in style and often used for blending
slides.11.questions.1.options.2: C. Its French name is Ugni Blanc, used as the base for Cognac
slides.11.questions.1.options.3: D. Its wines are usually very rich and complex
slides.11.questions.1.explanation: Trebbiano is Italy's most widely planted white grape, light in flavour and often used for blending. In France it is called Ugni Blanc and is the core base grape for Cognac. It is not usually known for richness or complexity.
slides.11.questions.2.question: In which region is Verdicchio's most famous area?
slides.11.questions.2.explanation: Verdicchio is the signature white grape of Marche, most famous as Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi DOC — crisp, with a herbal, bitter-almond finish, one of central Italy's most distinctive whites.
slides.11.questions.3.question: Garganega is the core grape of which famous white wine?
slides.11.questions.3.explanation: Garganega is the core grape of Veneto's Soave DOC (at least 70% by law), with white flowers, almond and honey; Soave Classico is especially fine and can rival top white Burgundy.
slides.11.questions.4.question: Which statements about Vermentino are correct? (Select all that apply)
slides.11.questions.4.options.0: A. Mainly from Sardinia and Liguria
slides.11.questions.4.options.1: B. Shows sea-breeze minerality and fresh herbal notes
slides.11.questions.4.options.3: D. Together with Nebbiolo, a signature grape of Piemonte
slides.11.questions.4.explanation: Vermentino is the signature white grape of Sardinia (Vermentino di Gallura DOCG) and Liguria; grown by the sea, it has a salty minerality and is an excellent choice with seafood. It has nothing to do with Piemonte.
